title: Irish heroes and heroines
html_source:
Joyce dismisses traditional heroes and idols-made-demigods, as he denigrates the myths and folklore that inevitably exaggerate their virtues and deny their vices. Again, the true heroes are like the one he presents to us in his great novel. It is Bloom with all his faults, fears, and eccentricities, whom he prototypes as the true Irish hero.

Joyce intended to have novel, style, myth and symbolism work together organically (Morris, N. A companion to James Joyce Ulysses, p22).
